name: Under the Dragon (Tarmac)
_name_doc: ONE-CHAIN section 3 (Kevin 2026-10-28): rally stages are '<Stage> (Gravel)' / '<Stage> (Tarmac)', two tracks (L8: surfaces.ini is per track). The engine era called it 'Rally Colorado - Under the Dragon (Tarmac)'. Installed as 'doooom Colorado — Under the Dragon (Tarmac)' (tools/ship_track.sh: ship.json ui_name_prefix + the layout's name).
_slug_doc: Kept from the engine era, as Sand Creek (sand_creek_raceway) and Exotics (exotics_racing_lvms) kept theirs: every kn5 is named for it and install_folder is it, so the chain's install parks the engine-era folder of the same name instead of standing beside it. ONE-CHAIN section 3's 'folder name with _' would be rally_under_the_dragon_tarmac; renaming is the main session's call (it orphans the old install).
_install_folder_doc: tools/ship_track.sh installs under content/tracks/<install_folder> (= the slug, ONE-CHAIN section 3); the previous install is parked in the archive
_version_doc: Keeps counting (ONE-CHAIN section 3). 0.1.0 was the engine-era config (never packaged: DEFINITION-OF-DONE 'no packaged build'); 0.2.0 keeps the pair in step with its gravel twin. Nothing has been built at 0.2.0.
author: doooom
_ui_series_doc: Kevin 2026-10-28: 'K10 is gone. doooom.' (was 'K10 Colorado Rally'). Content Manager shows '<ui_series> - <layout name>' (tools/ship_track.sh ui_name_prefix carries the same string)
_road_surface_doc: DELIBERATE FICTION - CR 109 is a dirt road in reality. Identical route, elevation and mesh to the gravel build; this key is the only difference.

source._doc: Whole stage lives on the OSM road network as County Road 109 - 10 ways, tertiary, surface=unpaved. Verified against Overpass 2026-07-24. See docs/STAGE-SOURCING.md.

route._roads_doc: The rally lists this stage as 'Under the Dragon - CR 109'. 25.6 km of mapped County Road 109, southwest of Rangely, pairing with Dragon Tail on CR 116 to the east.
route._start_at_doc: No start_at: without the event GPX we don't know which end the rally starts from, so the stage runs the mapped road in its OSM order. Set start_at to the real start once the GPX is in hand and the build will orient itself.
route._width_profile_doc: Rural table (3.0 m lanes, no urban parking/turn allowances). A graded county road is one narrow two-way surface, not a laned highway.

wide_corners._doc: 117° switchback at the stage's first climb. Gate-exact replication of drive_test's corner feasibility check (turn >110°, corner-core width <9 m) finds it at 6.5 m; a graded county hairpin is cut wider at the apex than the road it joins. 10 m per the Dragon Tail survey pattern. CORRECTED -31 m: stations were derived from gate output, which includes the lead-in; the engine adds _lead_offset assuming they do not. Measured flare centre landed at 802 for declared 771.

The big Douglas Creek switchback, five gate hits 2498–2519 peaking 137°. One flare at the centre covers the full cluster (full width ±18 m). 10 m, not 12 — Dragon Tail's second switchback proved 12 m overhangs its own embankment. CORRECTED -31 m: stations were derived from gate output, which includes the lead-in; the engine adds _lead_offset assuming they do not. Measured flare centre landed at 2539 for declared 2508.

113° hairpin on the final descent. CORRECTED -31 m: stations were derived from gate output, which includes the lead-in; the engine adds _lead_offset assuming they do not. Measured flare centre landed at 22562 for declared 22531.

_frame_doc: The chain's frame (ONE-CHAIN section 1, ledger 0060): local ENU metres, no mirror, no yaw, as Lake Murray 0.19.1. Stated explicitly so tools/ship_track.sh's FRAME check reads 'False 0.0' from the config itself and scripts.geometry.projection never writes the key back.
_ground_doc: Constructed corridor (false), not natural_ground, on this pass (2026-11-01) - against ONE-CHAIN section 4's rally_stage row, deliberately. The engine's natural path (build_mesh: ribbon.road_shoulder bank_hold, a 2 m blend band, 'corridor machinery OFF') skips the measured-guard lip pass and the shoulder drape; Milford tried it on 2026-10-28 and drive_test failed on 31 lidar banks at the pavement edge, which is why every chain circuit but Exotics runs constructed; and the constructed path is the one these stages passed all four gates on (ledger 0014). Rehearsed offline 2026-11-01 on Dragon Tail (Gravel)'s engine-era cached data (40 m grid, no corridor field), drive_test: constructed 0 ground-on-top, 237 severe steps, 64.5 bumps/km, FAIL on 2 floating parapet columns only; natural_ground 1,836 ground-on-top, 449 severe, 80.2 bumps/km. Flip this key once the Windows draft (with data/corridor.elev.json, the near-native 3DEP the natural path depends on) is green constructed, and compare.
_loop_doc: POINT-TO-POINT. A rally stage has two ends and is driven once (L11): the grid goes at the start of the road (here the north-east end, CR 109's OSM order), AC_TIME_0 (AC's start/finish) goes at the far south-west end as the finish, and the splits divide the run between them (scripts/geometry/dummies.py).
_osm_road_widths_doc: Off. OSM carries no lane count for an unpaved county road, so the lane-derived widths would be guesses dressed as data. A flat 6.5 m matches a graded two-track county road.

road_markings._doc: Paved fiction gets paint: a rural two-way road reads wrong without a centreline.

kerb._doc: No racing kerbs on a public dirt road - the edge is loose gravel into sagebrush.

runoff._doc: Run-off here is dirt, scrub and drop-off, not a paved apron.

road_profile._doc: Elevation is 100% real USGS 3DEP along the route - 1,833-2,216 m (6,017-7,270 ft) over the stage. max_grade_pct 18 clears the real steepest measured pitch (17.5%); the default 6% cap would flatten the mesa climbs and float the road over the drainages. Nothing hand-authored: no dips, no cambers, the terrain provides them.

scenery._doc: Pinyon-juniper woodland - the real vegetation of the Rio Blanco mesas at 5,000-7,000 ft. NOT the bare sagebrush flat an earlier pass assumed, and not a Front Range spruce forest either: continuous short-conifer woodland over the slopes and mesa tops, thinning into sage where the road drops into the drainages. Billboards carry the mass out to 300 m; real 3D pine geometry fills the corridor the driver actually reads. All of it bakes into the kn5 from bundled assets - nothing here depends on external models that could go missing.
scenery._fill_bias_doc: 1.5, not the Lariat's 2.4: pinyon-juniper spreads evenly across a slope rather than crowding the verge, so the bias toward the road is gentle.
scenery._tree_cap_doc: Billboards are ~12 verts each, so 40-60k of them cost under 1 M verts and are what makes the mesa read as continuous woodland. This is the immersion lever - NOT the 3D count, which is 4,006 verts per instance and blew environment.obj to 341 MB at 1,167 trees.

forest3d._doc: Real 3D trees only where the driver reads them - within 45 m of the road, 500 of them. Scale 0.8-1.7 on a 4.31 m module = 3.4-7.3 m trees, pinyon/juniper height (the Lariat's 2.2-4.2 would put 18 m alpine pines on a high-desert mesa). The cap is a hard budget: the module is 4,006 verts, so 500 instances is already ~2 M verts of forest.

scenery._bush_doc: Sagebrush and rabbitbrush under and between the trees - the understory that makes the woodland floor read right.

treefx._doc: OFF. TreeFX renders third-party .bin models we do not have, and a species with no model is exactly the 'tree manifest missing' failure. The forest above is baked geometry + billboards from bundled assets, so it ships with the track and cannot go missing.

scenery._fill_tree_h_doc: 3.5-7.5 m billboards. The engine default is 8-16 m (mature montane ponderosa, the Lariat's forest); pinyon and juniper on a 6,000 ft mesa are short and bushy. Matches the forest3d scale range so the two layers read as one woodland.

lighting._presets_doc: The rally runs mid-July; noon is the honest high-desert look (harsh, overhead, short shadows).
lighting._grassfx_doc: CSP-native 3D grass on the ground mesh - no external models, so nothing to go missing. This is what makes the verge read as dry scrub.

light_pollution._note: Rangely is a small town 25 km away across empty mesa - the night sky here is essentially dark.

1GRASS._doc: Dry high-desert dirt, not green grass. Mesh stays 1GRASS so physics, audits and GrassFX are untouched.

layouts.name: Under the Dragon (Tarmac)
layouts.run: Point to point, north-east to south-west along County Road 109 (the mapped road's OSM order)
layouts._doc: The one layout: CR 109 in its OSM order, north-east (39.8628, -108.9059, toward Rangely) to south-west (39.7466, -109.0495). Which end the rally starts from is unknown without the event GPX (route._start_at_doc). ONE-CHAIN section 3: a rally stage's surfaces are two TRACKS (L8), never two layouts.

_ui_tags_doc: 'circuit' first, deliberately: Content Manager refuses Race and Track Day sessions on a track not tagged 'circuit' (scripts/ac/track_folder.py ui_track_json adds it only on a loop), and L11's timing (the grid at the start, AC_TIME_0 at the finish) posts a stage time only in a session whose clock starts at the green: a one-lap Race. Practice / Hotlap arm the clock on the first AC_TIME_0 crossing, which on a stage is the finish. To be confirmed in the seat (does a 1-lap Race post the stage time?).
ui_description: Paved (fictional) point-to-point rally stage near Rangely, Colorado, built from real OpenStreetMap county-road geometry and USGS 3DEP elevation. Drive it once, start to finish - it is a stage, not a lap.
_terrain_cell_doc: The road is 6.5 m wide; the engine default gives ~10 m cells here, so a terrain triangle can span the whole carriageway. 8 m target -> x5 upsample -> ~8 m cells and ~1.46 M verts. x7 (5.7 m cells, 2.87 M verts) ran the mesh build out of memory and left a truncated track.obj, so the budget is capped deliberately.
readme_about: Real roads from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation: County Road 109 south-west of Rangely, Colorado, 25.7 km point to point (the rally's 'Under the Dragon - CR 109'). A stage is driven once, start to finish - not a lap.
_chain_doc: 2026-11-01, the chain pass (ONE-CHAIN section 4 row 6), DEPRIORITISED (_deprioritised). The engine-era tarmac config had drifted from its twin (no corridor_refine_factor, the ledger 0014 float fix; Under the Dragon also no route.wide_corners, so its three switchbacks would have been undrivable at 6.5 m); every geometry key is now the gravel twin's, and the pair differ only in what road_surface forks (L8, docs/RALLY-CONVENTIONS.md: name, slug, road_surface, road_markings, ui text and tags). Changed for the chain: name and ui_series (the name set), version 0.2.0, install_folder (= slug), the frame stated (mirror_x false, true_north_rotation_deg 0.0), natural_ground stated, one `stage` layout carrying its name and run text, 'circuit' in ui_tags (_ui_tags_doc), readme_about (the packed README otherwise says '... km a lap'). Unchanged and still read by the draft: source, route (roads, bbox, start_at, wide_corners), loop false (L11), default_width_m 6.5, road_profile.max_grade_pct 18, kerb / runoff / road_text off, road_markings, the terrain keys, texture_overrides, road_surface (scripts/ac/pbr.load_overrides forks the 1ROAD texture, track_folder.surfaces_ini the physics). INERT through the chain: scenery.* was read by the retired environment stage (scripts/environment/build_env.py), which the chain never runs - the pinyon-juniper woodland, rock cuts and everything else on the land are authoring (AUTH_* in loop.blend), owed. The rehearsal and what the Windows run reads first: ship.json _owed / _windows_first. Terrain (L3b): the 40 m 3DEP grid is 336 x 330 nodes (a 13 x 13 km box): x5 (2.76 M) and x4 (1.77 M) exceed terrain_vertex_budget 1.6 M, so build_mesh takes x3 = 13.3 m coarse cells (994 k verts); corridor_refine_factor 7 (corridor_stencil_factor 0.32) refines the 10,161 pavement quads to 1.9 m - finer than the 6.5 m road, near the chain circuits' 1.25-1.5 m. Left as the engine era tuned it (ledger 0014); raising the budget to 1.8 M would buy 10 m coarse cells at ~+0.8 M verts, not tried.
